questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had visited Italy quite a few times with familiy throughout my life and always enjoyed my time there, so I was excited to try to live there. Also, I was more interested in the courses than at other universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I made some great friends while I was there, so I highly recommend it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, and you could always write to the host university if you were confused about anything. Although their answers weren't always as clear as I would have liked, they still helped tremendously with calming my nerves.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been told how to get a metro card that would save me quite a bit of money during my stay but the info on that were given via mail before my exchange period started, so I don't know if it counts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was not much of an orientation but the host university were always ready to answer any questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not too difficult to find housing but prices increase the closer you get to the start of the semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Try to find housing as early as possible but expect it to a little expensive if you don't get housing through the university.
700-800 euros per month is pretty standard in my experience. There were some that paid higher but they also found housing later. You can also search for dorms that are directly connected to the host university (which is what I did).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to register for the courses but it was difficult to find courses that fit into the same schedule and did not overlap.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Search for courses in subjects you find interesting -> check to see if they offer during the semester or trimester of your stay (for me it was either 1st semester or trimester) -> check to see if I meet the prerequisites for admission to the course -> apply for pre-approval for all the courses (around 70 ects in total by the end for me) -> receive the course calendar and check which courses fit together and do not overlap (this can be quite difficult) -> register for the courses that fit into my schedule via university website (expect not to be able to accomodate all your first choices)
ps. also check for overlap in the exam calendar but at the University of Milan you can take exams in both January and December, so this shouldn't be a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a person you could contact at the host institution who helped a lot, and was willing to answer all my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not take any classes I did not want but I also couldn't fit in all my first choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get pre-approval for a lot of courses to save yourself some stress leading up to the start of your exchange stay, but it worked out in the end, so I wouldn't worry to much as you can always get more courses pre-approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not have too much difficulty with the level of my courses but my courses also had low/no prerequisites for admission.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
A lecture is, in my experience, 1,5 hour of straight talking and no breaks.

Not as many exercises as I was used to, so it was mostly lectures but this varied between courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Employment, Inequalities and Discrimination in The Global Labour Market, 
2) Human Development and Mobility in A Changing World, 
3) Business History, 
4) Conflict Management and Negotiation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Employment, Inequalities and Discrimination in The Global Labour Market" and also "Conflict Management and Negotiation"

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My dorm had a cafeteria where I could buy food but if I wanted to cook myself then I had to buy my own pots, pans, plates, cutlery etc. (I didn't do this so the cost is not included)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Metro card is quite cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Erasmus Student Network had a lot of events but I did not attend any.

I do not remember any offers from the University regarding clubs and such.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Received an email about a classical concert due to some anniversary.
Received the occasional email regarding other events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Concert at Teatro alla Scala, travelling

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See a game at the San Siro

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Events by Erasmus Student Network and talk to people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No popcorn at the movie theater (although not sure if this is specific to the one we visited).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Good food that wasn't all that expensive.

We once got complementary red wine at another restaurant, and a friend at my dormitory arrived at a party with a bottle of wine from his home town.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing early to avoid unnecassary costs, cheap all-you-can-eat sushi, and no need to stress too much about course registration and exams and such.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Watch Inter Milan matches instead of AC Milan because AC Milan don't score any goals.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Made some great friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing because I was pretty determined to stay at a dorm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Exchange stay in Italy is highly recommended.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
